=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- agents.md:line ~75 (Claude-fixer mode summary) | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: agents.md now claims both "the conflict resolver and the push / re-trigger tail run only for a pre-review conflict that touches `.claude/**`." CLAUDE.md §26.H describes the same restriction for the conflict resolver and review-blocked judge but does NOT mention the push/re-trigger tail being scoped in the same way. Either agents.md is adding a new behavioral claim that CLAUDE.md never ratified, or it is contradicting CLAUDE.md by omission.
  WHY: An AI agent reading agents.md to plan a fix on a `claude/*` PR will assume the push/re-trigger tail is also restricted to protected-path pre-review conflicts; on a non-protected pre-review conflict the agent may defer the follow-up dispatch that the workflow would normally trigger, stranding the PR.
- scripts/review_claude_fixer_judge.py:lines 338-344 (verdict_body) | confidence=[1]
  PROBLEM: `reason = _one_line(ruling["reason"]).replace("|", "\\|")` re-applies `_one_line` to a value that `decide()` already collapsed to one line via the same helper on line 204. The double-`_one_line` is idempotent (`" ".join(s.split())` is a no-op on already-collapsed input) but obscures intent and costs an extra split/join per ruling in the table render.
  WHY: No runtime defect — `_one_line` is idempotent and `replace("|", "\\|")` still escapes pipes. This is a readability issue only.
- .claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:lines 803-805 (retry_after_minutes) | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The new test `test_held_retry_minutes_survive_an_infinite_value` covers `inf`, `-inf`, `1e999` but not `nan`. `float("nan")` parses successfully and `int(float("nan"))` raises `ValueError` (caught by the existing `except`), so the behaviour is correct — but the regression test does not pin it.
  WHY: Setting `CLAUDE_CHECK_IN_HELD_RETRY_MINUTES=nan` would currently fall through to 180, but the test would not catch a future break in that contract.
- scripts/review_claude_fixer_judge.py:line 81 (TRUSTED_COMMENT_ASSOCIATIONS) | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The new `TRUSTED_COMMENT_ASSOCIATIONS = ("OWNER", "MEMBER", "COLLABORATOR")` is a sibling of the existing rejection-comment author rule in `scripts/review_autofix_step_claude_fixer_handoff.sh` (per the inline comment) but is a separate literal — there is no shared constant or contract test pinning them to stay equal.
  WHY: A maintainer who edits one trust set but not the other would create exactly the inconsistency the new test is meant to prevent; nothing in the diff ties them together.

- scripts/review_claude_fixer_evidence.py:head_repository guard at lines 295-299
  PROBLEM: The `or ""` fallback silently treats a missing `full_name` as same-repo-vacuous-rejection; a comment one line up the file path in `verify`'s caller already logs which run it rejected but not why. If `head_repository` is present but lacks `full_name` (a documented GitHub API quirk for some App-originated runs), the caller cannot distinguish a fork from a malformed response.
  SUGGESTED MINIMAL FIX: When `head_repository` is a dict but lacks `full_name`, log one `::warning::` line naming the run id before rejecting (`return reject("untrusted_caller_ref: missing head_repository.full_name")`). Lets an operator see the failure mode without changing the close-fail behavior.
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2
- scripts/review_claude_fixer_judge.py:_one_line at lines 157-158
  PROBLEM: `str(value or "")` collapses any falsy value to the empty string before split/join, which means a model that returns `False` or `0` for an action silently becomes `""` and falls through to the unruled-findings branch.
  SUGGESTED MINIMAL FIX: Wrap `_one_line` with an explicit `isinstance` check that returns `""` for `None` and `bool`, otherwise the existing `str(...)` path. Keeps the idempotency benefit for str input and documents the boolean case.
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
